claim: DR47-6's chosen fold (apply computeStructuralEdit n times, steps 2..n passing no baseline) is not expressible against the shipped types, and the only type-legal reading of it makes every n >= 2 drag fail.
evidence: StructuralEditIntent is `{ op: BaselinedWireVerb; expect: StructuralBaseline } | { op: 'insert-child'; expect: null }` — expect is required and non-null for move-up/move-down, and computeStructuralEdit's params are StructuralEditIntent & {...}. parseExpectForOp refuses a move request without a baseline outright. Only the lower-level moveAdjacent takes expect optionally, and the plan explicitly forbids folding at that level because it would mint a second engine entry point. Re-threading step 1's baseline is not a workaround: step 1's splice invalidates it, so every n >= 2 drag would 409 — the plan says as much itself. The shipped call site also carries a design note against exactly this recombination: the verb and its expect are spread from ONE value, so the pair the parser proved cannot be taken apart and recombined. The lead independently re-opened the type and confirmed both arms.
impact: The phase's one-gesture-one-undo mechanism — the owner's binding 2026-08-27 ruling, with no permitted fallback — has no buildable shape as ruled. The lane reaches S47-4, finds the primary untyped, and its only in-plan escape is EG-2's alternate mechanism, which the plan demotes to a branch. The no-new-write-class argument also enumerates the surfaces that stay byte-identical without pricing a widening of StructuralEditIntent / computeStructuralEdit's params, a shipped exported type on the write path.
required_correction: Rule how steps 2..n satisfy the type. Either promote the per-step deriveStructuralBaseline re-derivation to the PRIMARY mechanism — type-legal, and arm B's own between-step work — and re-mark the current alternate; or rule the widening of StructuralEditIntent's move arm to an optional expect explicitly, price it inside the no-new-write-class argument, and add it to acceptance 23's byte-identity list as a named reviewed exception. Either way restate 'steps 2..n pass no baseline' so it names a call the shipped types admit.

claim: Acceptances 46 and 50 — the only two gates over the phase's worst reachable outcome (a structural write against an element the user never touched) — under-specify their fixture so both can read green under their own RED-when mutation. CONVERGENT: the critic lane reached this independently.
evidence: 46 drives a lost-terminal gesture on A then a same-pointer gesture on a different element B in an eligible parent, and asserts the POST carries B's oid OR no POST is issued, never A's. Nothing requires A's parent to be eligible. Under the state table, engaged requires the eligibility module to ADMIT, so with A in an ineligible parent the mutated arm reaches refused, issues zero POSTs, and the disjunctive assertion is satisfied — green under the mutation. The stated Path silently assumes a POST exists in the mutated arm. Acceptance 50 has the same hole: a line is painted only if A's parent is eligible and A's tracker is armed, neither stated, and its Path omits the eligibility ADMIT that sits between engagement and any paint. The critic adds a fixture contradiction: if A's parent IS made eligible and gesture 1 crosses the engage threshold, gesture 1 is engaged and has painted a line whose terminals never arrive, so nothing tears that paint down — the plan rules the tracker's lifetime and the swallow cell's drain on that path but never the affordance PAINT's lifetime.
impact: This is the scenario the plan calls the worst defect the phase can ship, and the pre-mortem routes its entire prevention to these two gates. If both are green in the hazardous state, DR47-14 clauses 1 and 2 ship unverified — the identical failure mode that let round 3's acceptance 46 pass a review round.
required_correction: State in both criteria that A sits in a parent passing all three parts of DR47-7, that A's press is plain, and that A's source index and the drop index differ, so the mutation genuinely issues A's POST. For 46, drop the 'or no POST is issued' disjunct or add a leg asserting exactly one POST in the mutated arm. Re-state both Paths to carry the eligibility ADMIT and the drop-index-differs clause as traced steps. Rule the paint's lifetime on a lost terminal, and say which, because 50's assertion depends on it.

claim: Acceptance 8's Path rests on a behaviour the plan never rules: that a seeded-but-not-armed tracker accumulates travel and evaluates the reorder threshold. CONVERGENT: the architect lane reached this independently.
evidence: 8's mutation is to make the reorder tracker write maxTravelRef when the reorder threshold is crossed, and its assertion is the swallow verdict on a Shift drag past 4 px. For that mutation to execute during a Shift drag the tracker must compute its own travel and cross the engage threshold while armed is false. The state table gives seeded no travel and no threshold column — it enters refused/engaged only from armed — and DR47-14 clause 2 gates accumulation on the primary button alone, never stating that accumulation is independent of armed. An implementation that short-circuits the move handler on !armed is fully conformant with the plan while making 8's mutation unreachable on the asserted gesture. The round-3 split fixed the tracker's EXISTENCE under Shift, not its ACCUMULATION.
impact: Acceptance 8 is the only gate pinning that the widened stream leaves the shipped travel number byte-identical, and S47-2's failure behaviour makes it the stop boundary halting the highest-risk edit in the phase. A non-firing stop boundary means the two consumers' compatibility ships unmeasured, guarding a regression to the shipped Shift/multi-select click swallow against Principle 1.
required_correction: Rule explicitly that travel accumulation and reorder-threshold evaluation are modifier-blind — only clause 2's button condition gates them, and armed gates entry into refused/engaged and nothing earlier — add that cell to the state table, and re-state acceptance 8's Path against it. Or, if accumulation is instead ruled armed-gated, replace acceptance 8's mutation with one that executes on a plain ineligible-parent gesture and re-trace.

claim: Section 3.4b names no surviving home for the trailing-click swallow verdict, and the one cell it does name is provably dead before the click arm reads it — which decides whether acceptance 15 leg (b) can fire at all.
evidence: Section 3.4b rules that reorder's cell is the gesture cell the shield already owns, so there is one new read and no new lifetime contract. The only gesture cell the shield owns is activeTravelGestureRef, and it is nulled from onGestureEnd on the document-capture pointerup — before the click the swallow is supposed to eat. Two readings follow: the verdict lives in that cell, in which case it is always null at click time, the swallow never fires, and acceptance 15 leg (b)'s hazard cannot occur so its RED-when moves no assertion; or the verdict lives in a new ref with a press-drain / click-consume lifetime, which is exactly a new lifetime contract and contradicts the sentence quoted. The plan never says which, and pre-mortem S6's residual reads as endorsing the first.
impact: The first reading ships DR47-4 as a no-op — the trailing click after every committed reorder resolves a selection against the parent, the outcome section 3.4 exists to prevent — and simultaneously makes acceptance 15(b), the only gate over the drain, non-discriminating. Approval would route a lane to an unfalsifiable gate over a shipped behaviour change.
required_correction: Rule the verdict's home explicitly: a named ref cell separate from activeTravelGestureRef, written at release when the drop index differs from the source index, read one-shot in the click arm, and drained unconditionally at every press. Delete or restate the 'no new lifetime contract' sentence, since the drain ruling is one, and re-state acceptance 15 leg (b)'s Path against that cell.
